FIG. 7. Extracting the transient peak positions of the graphene π-band. a) EDCs extracted from Fig. 2c at the M point of graphene for negative pump-probe delay and at t = 0.07 ps fitted with a Shirley background and two Gaussian peaks (red line). The dotted vertical lines mark the peak positions for negative pump-probe delay. The low-energy peak indicated in light blue corresponds to the graphene valence band. b) MDC extracted from Fig. 2a at E − EF = 0.2 eV, fitted with a Lorentzian and a constant offset (red).

FIG. 1. LEED image of WS2-graphene heterostructure. LEED image taken with an electron energy of Ekin = 68 eV. The grey hexagon marks the diffraction spots of graphene. Blue and orange hexagons indicate the diffraction spots from WS2 islands with twist angles of 0◦ and 30◦ relative to the graphene layer, respectively.

FIG. 5. Extracting the transient position of the WS2 valence band. a) EDCs at the Kpoint of WS2 for a twist angle of 0° extracted from Fig. 2a for negative pump-probe delay (bottom) and at t = 0.27 ps (top) fitted with a constant background and three Gaussian peaks (red line). The dotted vertical lines mark the peak positions for negative pump-probe delay. The coloured Gaussians illustrate the fit contributions from the three bands. b) Same as a) but for a twist angle of 30°.

FIG. 4. Transient band structure. a) Transient band positions of WS2 CB (top) and VB (bottom). b) Transient band gap. c) Charging shift of WS2. Light (dark) data points belong to the WS2 VB (CB). d) Charging shift of graphene. Colored lines are exponential fits as described in the Supplemental Material. Black lines in a) are calculated from the fits in b) and c).
FIG. 6. Extracting the transient position of the WS2 conduction band. EDC at k = 1.3 Å −1 extracted from Fig. 2d at t = 0.13 ps together with Gaussian fit.

FIG. 3. Population dynamics. a) Gain above the Fermi level (red) and loss below the Fermi level (blue) inside the Dirac cone as obtained by integrating the counts over the areas marked by the red and blue box in Fig. 2b. b) Transient population of the WS2 CB at K for both 0◦ and 30◦ islands. c) Gain above the equilibrium position of the WS2 VB for both 0◦ and 30◦ islands. Data points in c) and d) were obtained by integrating the counts over the areas marked by the respective boxes in Figs. 2b and d. Continuous lines are exponential fits as described in the Supplemental Material. Vertical dashed lines indicate temporal overlap of pump and probe pulses, horizontal dashed lines indicate the equilibrium levels.
